name: Elgi Equipments Ltd
title: Elgi Equipments Ltd - 522074 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Elgi FY26 revenue grew about 12% and PBT about 17%, but management flagged metal-commodity cost pressure and a 2.5-3% price correction in June.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 sales up about 12% and PBT up 17%, with consolidated revenue close to Rs 4,000 crore, though EBITDA was held back by a 16% rise in employee cost tied to US/Europe reorganisation and a one-time settlement, plus product mix and tariff effects. Management said it generated 100% of EBITDA as cash even after excluding the US property sale proceeds. Europe moved to breakeven in Q4 after cost realignment, but was loss-making for the full year. The outlook for Q1 FY27 is for top-line growth similar to FY26 and bottom-line growth roughly similar in percentage terms, with near-term caution on West Asia and commodity prices.

financial_highlights.value: management said it should have been about Rs 2,100 million before employee cost impact
financial_highlights.change: reported EBITDA increased; no exact figure given
up 16% YoY, incl. one-time settlement cost
up about 8% YoY on IT investments

financial_highlights.value: 100% of EBITDA as cash, normalised for property sale

segments.name: Compressors
segments.commentary: Mix broadly stable versus automotive equipment; compressor business split about 50-50 between India and rest of world, described as roughly 90-10 in one framing. Low-cost range for India launching September 2026, rest of world next year.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Cost realignment complete; Q4 FY26 EBITDA breakeven, FY26 loss. Management expects marginal profitability in FY27 and is not investing more capital in Europe.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Industrial business grew exceptionally well; Pattons Medical grew; portable compressors hit by cyclical trough; distribution improved in the last two quarters.

segments.name: Vacuum
segments.commentary: Entered via a licence agreement with DVP as a low-cost learning platform; described as a 10-12 year programme, not a near-term growth driver.

segments.name: Rotair
segments.commentary: Inventory reduced in response to muted growth.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 top-line growth expected to be similar to or slightly better than FY26 growth rate; bottom-line growth roughly the same in percentage terms.
Price correction of roughly 2.5-3% planned for June 2026, after commodity costs rose; about 80% of projected material cost increase already occurred in Q1.
Europe expected to be marginally profitable in FY27 at a realistic case.
Capex FY27 around Rs 200 crore: Rs 120-130 crore for the factory relocation to new plant plus about Rs 70 crore of balancing capex.
Inventory levels expected to keep improving into FY27; forecasting accuracy at 60-70% with target around 90%.
IT and process digitisation programme to continue for the next three to four years.
capex_capacity: FY26 total capex about Rs 1.5 billion (per analyst's recollection in Q&A); FY27 plan about Rs 200 crore.
Progressive shift of factory from city to new plant to absorb Rs 120-130 crore in FY27.
Balancing capex about Rs 70 crore in FY27.
Management noted desire to spend is much higher than capability to spend.
No further capital investment planned in Europe; growth to come organically, including entry into Germany.
demand_pricing: Volume growth around 3-4% across verticals in FY26; pricing gains small; Demand=Match launched September 2025 with a very small contribution so far; FX a significant contributor.
India inquiry levels strong across verticals, but conversion timing is elongating; caution driven mainly by West Asia uncertainty.
Price correction of 2.5-3% already in market (projected for FY27 cost increases), further correction planned for June given commodity moves.
US tariffs now around 25% (down from 50%), applied under a different US regulation section; refund of past tariffs under discussion.
Chinese low-cost compressor makers are churning the bottom end globally; management says overall industry structure is otherwise stable.
Demand drivers: industrial growth and capacity additions; US reshoring; data-centre ancillary compressed air demand but no direct data-centre business.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 blended realisation growth, and what price increases are needed in FY27 to hold gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 3-4%; pricing was small; FX was a significant contributor. Projected cost increases implied 2.5-3% price correction, already introduced, with a further correction planned for June as about 80% of expected material cost increases already occurred in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off in other expenses, and was it linked to shared services?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a one-off; increase reflects India go-to-market investment and IT spend, primarily the PLM investment.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indian capex recovery accelerating, steady or slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Inquiry levels remain strong, but conversion is slower; West Asia uncertainty is the main caution rather than price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US tariff situation and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs are around 25% now versus 50% earlier; refund talks ongoing but too early to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company responding to Chinese low-cost compressors?
qa_highlights.answer: Low-cost range validated; launch in India in September, rest of world next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory reduction and forecasting progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Low-hanging fruit done in Elgi and Rotair regions; distribution businesses in Australia and US still to address; forecast accuracy 60-70%, targeting 90%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe outlook and what is the FY26 EBITDA loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 breakeven; FY26 a loss, exact figure not disclosed. Expect marginal profitability in FY27 in a realistic case.

risks_watch: Metal commodity price volatility; management is monitoring monthly and said it does not want a repeat of post-COVID margin hit.
West Asia conflict and energy security affecting order conversion timing in India and Middle East.
Demand elasticity to the June price correction is uncertain.
Employee cost and IT/process investments (three to four years) could keep opex elevated.
US tariff regime shifts and possible refunds.
Chinese low-cost competition at the bottom of the market; launch timing in September 2026 to watch.
Europe market growth muted; breakeven rather than strong profit in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and cash generation, but cautious on the outlook, citing West Asia uncertainty and commodity price swings. Management was candid about the FY26 EBITDA gap from employee cost and was less specific on the Europe loss and forex gains, deferring some numbers to the investor relations team.
key_quotes: We will correct prices when there is a demand to do so.
The last time we were kind of blindsided, we didn't watch this carefully and we took a hit on our profitability. We're going to learn from that.
We are not interested in investing more capital in Europe at this point in time.
So, we have our, you know, the larger project of progressively shifting our factory from the city to the new plant that will absorb about 120, 130 crores this year, right?

Low-cost compressor range for India launch

growth.why: Management guides Q1 FY27 top-line growth similar to or slightly better than FY26's roughly 12%, and bottom-line growth in line in percentage terms, backed mainly by a 2.5-3% price correction (about 80% of cost increase already hit in Q1) and volume growth of 3-4%, with only partial specifics given and a Rs 200 crore FY27 capex plan including a Rs 120-130 crore factory relocation.
